chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Mu'ttab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'Go and give the Fitra on behalf of our dependents, and give on behalf of the slaves, and gather them together and do not leave any of them, for if you leave a person from them, I would fear the loss for him.' I said: 'And what is the loss?' He said: 'Death.'

key_terms.الرَّقِيق: The slaves (plural of 'abd), referring to those under ownership
key_terms.الْفَوْت: Al-Fawt (loss/missed opportunity), specifically interpreted here as death
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitra (Zakat al-Fitr), the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on giving Fitra for slaves and dependents in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs his companion to ensure the Fitra is distributed for all dependents and slaves, emphasizing collective inclusion to avoid 'Al-Fawt' (loss), which he explicitly defines as death. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the completeness of the obligation extends to every individual member of the household, including slaves, and that neglecting any part risks spiritual or physical detriment. The instruction underscores the communal responsibility in fulfilling religious dues, ensuring no one is left behind in the act of purification.
